questions.question: Unwanted but often unavoidable pharmacodynamic effects that occur at normal therapeutic doses, and are generally predictable from a drug's known pharmacological profile, are classified as:
questions.explanation: Side effects are unwanted but often unavoidable pharmacodynamic effects occurring at therapeutic doses — generally not serious, predictable from the drug's pharmacological profile, and often improved by reducing the dose (e.g. dry mouth from atropine's antisecretory action).
questions.sourceBook: KD Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: Type 1 diabetes mellitus is characterised by:

options.D: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells and insulin deficiency

questions.explanation: Usually presents in young patients with polyuria, weight loss and ketosis.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine; Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In the standing position the line of gravity passes:

options.A: Through the centre of the ankle
options.D: Anterior to the ankle and knee axes and posterior to the hip axis

questions.explanation: Hence the ankle plantar flexors work to prevent forward sway.

questions.question: In pharmacology, a drug that activates a receptor to produce an effect similar to the physiological signal molecule is called a/an:
questions.explanation: An agonist activates a receptor to produce an effect similar to that of the natural (physiological) signal molecule. An antagonist, by contrast, prevents an agonist's action without producing an effect of its own.
questions.sourceBook: KD Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology
